claims.claim: Exact certificate characterization: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor exactly when it has six pairwise-disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4 such that A and B are anticomplete and every other pair of sets has an edge between it. Consequently detection is in NP and has an O(7^n n²) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: The branch-set statement is exactly the definition of an induced-minor model specialized to K6 minus one edge. Contraction preserves every required inter-set adjacency, while the sole forbidden adjacency is preserved precisely by A and B being anticomplete. Conversely, deleting unused vertices and contracting spanning trees of the six connected sets produces exactly the target. Seven labels enumerate all possible certificates, and all conditions are checkable in O(n²).
claims.witness: A seven-label assignment—unused, A, B, C1, C2, C3, or C4—is a polynomial-size certificate; contracting each nonempty connected labeled set witnesses the induced minor.
claims.search_method: Direct definition-level proof audit with both implications and complexity accounting; no external search.

claims.claim: Let q be the number of nonedges of G. Detection is fixed-parameter tractable in q, in time O(7^(2q+3)n²), and undecided instances have at most 2q+3 vertices. In particular, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when q=O(log n).
claims.evidence: If q=0, every two disjoint nonempty sets have a cross-edge, so the exceptional anticomplete branches cannot exist. If q>0 and four universal vertices exist, they together with the endpoints of any nonedge induce K6 minus that edge. Otherwise at most three vertices are universal, and every other vertex is among the at most 2q endpoints of the q nonedges, giving n≤2q+3. Claim 0's algorithm then has the stated FPT time. For q=O(log n), 7^(2q+3)=n^{O(1)}.
claims.witness: For a nonedge uv and universal vertices x1,…,x4, the induced graph on {u,v,x1,…,x4} is exactly K6 minus uv; in the residual case, the endpoint cover of all nonuniversal vertices proves the kernel bound.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive case analysis on q and the number of universal vertices; no external search.

claims.claim: On chordal graphs, K6 minus an edge is an induced minor if and only if it is already an induced subgraph. Thus chordal inputs can be decided in O(n^6) time by enumerating six vertices. The same argument works for Kt minus an edge for every fixed t≥3.
claims.evidence: Inside a branch model, the four core branches give four internally vertex-disjoint A–B paths. An inclusion-minimal A–B separator S disjoint from A∪B therefore has size at least four. In a chordal graph every minimal separator is a clique, and each of its two full components contains an S-complete vertex; the latter follows by maximizing the separator neighborhood in the component and using a shortest path to any missed separator vertex, which otherwise creates a chordless cycle. S-complete vertices x and y in the two components are nonadjacent, so x,y and any four vertices of S induce exactly K6 minus xy. Replacing four by t−2 proves the fixed-t statement. The reverse implication and O(n^6) enumeration are immediate.
claims.witness: The induced target is formed by two S-complete vertices in distinct full components of G−S and four vertices of the clique separator S.
claims.search_method: Independent minimal-separator proof, including the full-component lemma and the t−2 quantifier generalization; no external search.

claims.claim: There is an explicit polynomial-time classification on complete multipartite graphs. Let the part sizes be n1,…,nr. For every i with ni≥2, reserve two vertices of part i and put mi=ni−2 and mj=nj for j≠i. Accept exactly when, for some s∈{0,…,4} and some s distinct indices J⊆{1,…,r}\{i}, subtracting one from each mj with j∈J leaves counts whose complete multipartite graph has a matching of size at least 4−s. If the residual total is M and its largest part has size L, this matching size is min(⌊M/2⌋,M−L).
claims.evidence: Anticompleteness forces both exceptional branches into one independent part, and connectivity then forces each to be a singleton. Every core branch is either a singleton in a distinct outside part or meets at least two parts. A branch of the latter kind can be reduced to one cross-part edge without losing adjacency to either exception, any outside singleton, or another cross-part edge. Thus s singleton cores consume one vertex in each distinct part in J, while the remaining 4−s cores are exactly a matching in the residual complete multipartite graph. Conversely, every such selection supplies a model. Any matching has size at most ⌊M/2⌋ and M−L, and pairing vertices from different largest remaining parts attains their minimum.
claims.witness: Two reserved vertices of part i are A and B; the J vertices are singleton cores, and the residual matching edges are the remaining connected core branch sets.
claims.search_method: Normal-form reduction of arbitrary branch sets followed by an exact maximum-matching argument; no external search.

claims.claim: Given a tree decomposition of width w, detection is decidable in n·2^{O(w log w)} time; hence it is polynomial-time solvable on every fixed-width class supplied with such decompositions.
claims.evidence: The proposed nice-decomposition state contains exactly the information needed: seven-way bag labels, a connectivity partition for each branch label, unseen/active/completed status preventing disconnected reopening, and the constant fourteen required-adjacency bits. Introduce-edge nodes also reject every A–B edge. Forgetting the last representative of a component is sound because no forgotten vertex can connect above the separator; join partitions combine by transitive closure and reject two closed off-bag copies. The empty-root condition is equivalent to a complete six-branch certificate. There are at most 7^(w+1)·Bell(w+1) times a target-dependent constant states, and even quadratic join processing remains 2^{O(w log w)}, yielding the stated linear-in-n factor.
claims.witness: An accepting root state has all six labels completed exactly once, no forbidden A–B edge, and all fourteen required adjacency bits set.
claims.search_method: State-invariant, transition, join, acceptance, and state-count audit of the dynamic program; no external search.

claims.claim: A model cannot in general be normalized so that either endpoint of the missing edge has a singleton branch set. A 12-vertex counterexample consists of anticomplete paths A=a1a2a3a4 and B=b1b2b3b4, a clique C={c1,c2,c3,c4}, and exactly the additional edges aici and bici for i=1,…,4.
claims.evidence: The two paths and four clique singletons form the displayed model. In any model with singleton exceptional branch {x}, x needs four distinct core neighbors, so x must be a degree-five vertex ci. Its anticomplete mate is then an interval in one component of A−ai or B−bi. Exhaustion gives no interval with four external neighbors for i=2,3. For i=1,4, exactly eight symmetric singleton/interval pairs have at least four external neighbors; in each, the four cores must separately contain all four boundary vertices, one of which is isolated after deleting x and the interval. Its core would therefore be an isolated singleton and could not meet the other three cores.
claims.witness: For x=c1, the only A-side possibilities are {a2,a3}, with boundary {a1,a4,c2,c3}, and {a2,a3,a4}, with boundary {a1,c2,c3,c4}; a1 is isolated in both residual graphs. The other seven cases are symmetric and were enumerated exactly.
claims.search_method: Degree reduction, exhaustive connected-interval analysis, and exact reconstruction from the claim text.

claims.claim: In every subcubic graph, each exceptional branch set in a K6-minus-an-edge induced-minor model has at least two vertices and each of the four core branch sets has at least three vertices. Consequently every such model uses at least 16 vertices.
claims.evidence: For a connected k-vertex branch S in a subcubic graph, |δ(S)|=Σdeg(v)−2|E(S)|≤3k−2(k−1)=k+2. An exceptional branch needs boundary edges to four distinct core branches, hence k+2≥4 and k≥2. A core needs boundary edges to the other five branches, hence k+2≥5 and k≥3. Disjointness then gives at least 2+2+4·3=16 vertices.
claims.witness: The exact boundary inequality separately yields the sharp per-label lower bounds 2,2,3,3,3,3.
claims.search_method: Direct exact boundary-degree counting with all six target degrees checked; no external search.

claims.claim: The subcubic lower bound is tight: the following 16-vertex cubic graph contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor. Its six branch paths are A=a1a2, B=b1b2, and Ci=ci1ci2ci3 for i=1,…,4. Besides the path edges, add a1c11,a1c21,a2c31,a2c41, b1c11,b1c21,b2c31,b2c41, c12c22,c32c42,c13c33,c13c43,c23c33,c23c43, and no other edges.
claims.evidence: Exact reconstruction gives 16 vertices, 24 edges, and degree three at every vertex. A and B are connected and anticomplete. The first eight cross-branch edges meet every A/core and B/core pair, while the final six meet the six unordered pairs of core paths exactly once. Thus the six paths are a valid spanning model. Together with Claim 6's universal 16-vertex lower bound, this proves tightness.
claims.witness: The exact checker validates all degrees, disjoint connected branch paths, the missing A–B adjacency, and all fourteen required branch-pair adjacencies.
claims.search_method: Exact graph reconstruction and independent branch-model validation.

claims.claim: For ℓ≥1, let Xℓ be obtained by replacing every edge of the preceding 16-vertex cubic graph by a path of ℓ edges. Then Xℓ is connected and bridgeless, has 24ℓ−8 vertices, 24ℓ edges, maximum degree 3, cycle rank 9, and treewidth exactly 4, and contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor.
claims.evidence: The cubic base has 16 vertices and 24 edges and is connected and bridgeless. Uniform subdivision therefore gives V=16+24(ℓ−1)=24ℓ−8, E=24ℓ, maximum degree three, and cycle rank E−V+1=9; connectivity and bridgelessness are subdivision-invariant. Contracting each subdivided path restores the base and hence the target induced minor. The stated filled elimination order was recomputed and has maximum later degree four with the exact displayed sequence. Eliminating degree-two subdivision vertices first restores that order, proving tw(Xℓ)≤4. Since K6 minus an edge is a minor of Xℓ and has treewidth four, equality follows.
claims.witness: The base order has later degrees 3,3,3,3,4,4,3,4,4,4,4,4,3,2,1,0. Exact checks for ℓ=1,…,8 also reproduce the formulas, bridgelessness, cycle rank, and spanning target models.
claims.search_method: Symbolic subdivision accounting plus exact base-graph, elimination-order, and finite-instance checks.

claims.claim: Every K6-minus-an-edge induced-minor model in Xℓ is spanning. Consequently its largest branch set has at least 4ℓ−1 vertices. Thus branch-set size is unbounded even for subcubic hosts of the minimum possible maximum degree and treewidth.
claims.evidence: Let U be the branch-set union. Contracting its six connected branches to the target cannot increase cycle rank, so the connected induced subgraph Xℓ[U] has cycle rank at least β(K6−e)=14−6+1=9. Its cycle space embeds in the nine-dimensional cycle space of Xℓ. If U were proper, an omitted vertex would lie on a cycle because Xℓ is bridgeless; that cycle uses an edge outside Xℓ[U], proving the embedded subspace proper and hence of dimension at most eight, a contradiction. Thus U is spanning. Pigeonhole gives max branch size at least ceil((24ℓ−8)/6)=4ℓ−1. Maximum degree at most two cannot supply four boundary edges from a connected exceptional branch, and treewidth below four cannot contain the target minor, so both stated host bounds are minimal.
claims.witness: The cycle-rank equality β(Xℓ)=β(K6−e)=9 forces every model union to contain every cycle-space direction and therefore every vertex.
claims.search_method: Independent binary cycle-space argument, followed by exact pigeonhole and lower-bound calculations; explicit family premises were checker-validated.

claims.claim: For every integer ℓ≥1, let Fℓ consist of a clique Q={c0,c1,c2,c3}, two mutually anticomplete induced paths a0…a(3ℓ) and b0…b(3ℓ), and, besides the clique and path edges, exactly the edges ci-a(iℓ) and ci-b(iℓ) for i=0,1,2,3. Then Fℓ has maximum degree 5 and treewidth exactly 4, and it contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor.
claims.evidence: Each ci has its three clique edges and two attachment edges, while path vertices have degree at most three, so Δ(Fℓ)=5. The two full paths and the four singleton clique vertices give the target model. Eliminating either path from index 0 upward gives each eliminated vertex at most its successor and the clique vertices whose attachment positions have already been passed, totaling at most four later neighbors; after both paths, only Q remains. Hence tw(Fℓ)≤4. The displayed induced minor is also an ordinary K6−e minor, whose K5 subgraph gives treewidth at least four.
claims.witness: The exact checker validates the full-path model, maximum degree, and width-four elimination order for ℓ=1,…,12.
claims.search_method: Direct degree/model proof and symbolic filled-elimination analysis, supplemented by exact finite checks.

claims.claim: In Fℓ, the minimum, over all K6-minus-an-edge induced-minor models, of max(|A|,|B|) for the two exceptional nonadjacent branch sets is exactly ℓ+1. Consequently no constant depending only on the target can bound both exceptional branch sets, even on hosts of maximum degree 5 and the minimum possible treewidth 4.
claims.evidence: Two anticomplete branches cannot both meet the clique Q, so at least one exceptional branch S avoids Q. Since Fℓ−Q is two disjoint paths, S is an interval in one path. If it contains r attachment sites, at most r attachment edges and two path edges leave it. Four distinct core adjacencies require at least four boundary edges, so r≥2. Consecutive attachment sites are ℓ edges apart, hence |S|≥ℓ+1 and max(|A|,|B|)≥ℓ+1. Equality is attained by the two middle intervals and the four stated connected core sets: c1 and c2 alone, with c0 joined to both prefixes and c3 joined to both suffixes. Clique edges make all cores pairwise adjacent, and path-boundary or attachment edges connect each core to both exceptional intervals.
claims.witness: A={aℓ,…,a(2ℓ)} and B={bℓ,…,b(2ℓ)} have size ℓ+1; the prefix/c0, {c1}, {c2}, and suffix/c3 branches complete a spanning model. Exact interval exhaustion for ℓ=1,…,12 found minimum qualifying size ℓ+1.
claims.search_method: Universal boundary-edge lower bound plus explicit equality construction and exact interval checks.

target_evidence: The source asks for the unrestricted complexity classification and, if tractable, a polynomial-time algorithm. The draft labels itself PARTIAL and expressly states that the unrestricted classification remains open, so that resolution claim is accurate.
